The 2002 original full text is a named residual risk, rather than evidence of noncoverage.

originality.rationale: The assessed theorem is the joint noise-invariant covariance-sign classification, exact recoverable quotient and finite-sample inference bound for a single sampled tree path under unknown event-specific positively informative independent binary channels. The recent one-path source studies the distinct noiseless conditional-independence line graph, which is not invariant under measurement noise. Classic graph and covariance identities are explicitly credited. Existing noisy oncogenetic reconstructions do not directly cover the exclusive single-path sampling law; a 2002 original article remained inaccessible, creating a specific priority risk.
residual_risks: The 2002 Szabo–Boucher primary article was not read in full after unsuccessful lawful arXiv/open-access and institutional retrieval. Its exact theorem hypotheses merit later human comparison.
A broader literature on phylogeny, tree covariances and noisy latent-tree inference may contain an equivalent combination under a different name; search coverage cannot establish novelty.

Some individual proof ingredients are classical or elementary; the research value assessment rests on the combined exact model classification and practical unknown-heterogeneous-noise reconstruction boundary.

value.rationale: The finding supplies a natural complete covariance-sign feasibility classification, a precisely identified recoverable hierarchical quotient and a finite-sample guarantee in a difficult noisy observation regime where conditional-independence graph inference fails. Distinct from reconstructing a standard independent-branch oncogenetic tree, it supports a falsifiable noise-robust diagnostic for cross-sectional single-lineage data. It avoids arbitrary parameter slices and does not claim a minimax bound.
